not_established: A first divergence is the earliest established mismatch with an expectation. It is not a root cause; no causal relationship is asserted.
'No divergence observed' means no mismatch was established in the expectations and evidence actually evaluated. It does not show the system behaved correctly.
Expectations are exactly those supplied in the contract; none was derived from the recording.
JSON payloads, and CDR payloads that carry an embedded ros2msg schema (with the optional decoder installed), are decoded; other encodings and schema formats are not interpreted.
Clock domains are never merged or converted. The relation of MCAP log_time (declared basis: 'unknown') to wall-clock time or any other clock is not established.
Evidence integrity is as established by the inventory and by re-hashing each segment at investigation time; it is not a statement about truthfulness.
Live ROS 2 capture is not verified.

An event_response result compares mcap log_time, the recorder's receipt time, for both trigger and response. It is not the time an event physically occurred, and receipt order is not event order; the result says what the recorder received, not what the robot did.

A response is a later matching sample. It is not shown to be caused by the trigger. A response absent from the recording is not shown to have been unpublished: a silent publisher and a message that was published but not captured look the same in a recording.

A payload stamp (header.stamp) is the publisher's own claim about when something happened. Each payload clock is its own domain and is never compared with another clock or with log_time; no offset is inferred. For JSON payloads the ROS type of a stamp field cannot be verified, only its sec/nanosec structure; a stamp of zero is read as zero (it may be a simulation time or an unset stamp).
